criteria.intent: The new report, a second file beside csv-export-andthen-code-review-claude-2026-10-19.md, carries the header line `**Follows**: csv-export-andthen-code-review-claude-2026-10-19.md`.

The new report states a current state for both earlier findings: Finding 1 (the malformed amount escaping cli.main) as resolved, citing the ValueError handler in cli.main or tests/test_cli.py, and Finding 2 (the flat one-second retry pause) as still open.

Earlier Finding 2, which the earlier report's Remediation Status marks SURFACED, is listed in the new report with the mark SURFACED, and no `### Finding` block of the new report raises it again: none has the pause length, the flat pause, or the five-retry count as the defect it asks to fix. A separate finding whose defect is something else, such as which errors get retried, passes even when its evidence or impact cites the one-second pause or the five retries.
No `### Finding` block of the new report states that a malformed amount cell escapes cli.main as a traceback or exits 1; the fixed behavior is reported as resolved, never as a finding.

The new report's Coverage Matrix has a row for the fix diff (the ValueError handler in `cli.main` or `tests/test_cli.py`), a row for a caller of the changed code (`src/reporter/__main__.py` or `tests/journeys/journey_export.py`), and a row for the open retry-pause finding. It has no row whose surface is only untouched target code, such as the staging order in `pipeline.run` or the `--name` argument reaching `write_report`, and no `Partition strategy:` or `Partition map:` line. The earlier report carries `**Remediated**:`, so the run narrows to the fix diff, its callers, and the open findings instead of re-partitioning the target.
